section.title: Overview
section.prose:
A component is the single document class of the specification corpus: a versioned root element carrying a required status and an ordered list of blocks. This file is itself a component describing the vocabulary, so it exercises every block type. The block taxonomy is seeded from a proven manual chapter shape and Lean-style titled boxes
.

Each
defines its terms once and references them thereafter; the validator enforces define-once and resolution across the whole corpus. The
attribute is required.

section.title: Block types
section.definition: A paragraph of inline content: literal text, inline math such as tilde(mu) , term references, and cite references.

grammar.production: section | prose | judgements | grammar | rule | definition | diagram | code | example | list | table | references

section.prose:
The payload register of the two-register weave, exercised: dictionary, decision, and staging content authors as a
table; enumerated registers as a list; normative API surfaces as an api-role code block — the schema itself is the example — and section-granular links as refs. Each exists so a class of dense payload never has to flatten into prose.

table.caption: The payload blocks and links of the two-register weave

row.cell: caption, header row, body rows of inline cells
Dictionary, decision, mapping, and staging tables — never flattened to prose.
ordered flag, items with an optional bold lead
Enumerated registers: obligations, open questions, residual seams.
Normative API surfaces — typed signatures and data layouts, never executed.
Cross-component and section-granular links; the readability answer to density, validated like term and cite.

list.item: Every load-bearing artifact lives in a block.
Every block gets an introducing prose paragraph.

Density is answered by spreading out, explaining, and linking — as this section's
link illustrates — never by dropping.

diagram.caption: A component contains sections, which contain blocks.

section.diagram: #diagram( node((0,0), [component]), node((1,0), [section]), node((1,1), [block]), edge((0,0), (1,0), [contains], "->"), edge((1,0), (1,1), [contains], "->"), edge((0,0), (1,1), [reaches], "-->"), )

example.title: A code block anticipating output
example.prose: Code blocks structurally anticipate checked examples. The tool validates the shape of the expectation but never executes it.
